title: Back on Planet Earth: eight months in space
summaryFr: Quatre astronautes, dont la Française Sophie Adenot, reviennent de l'ISS après presque huit mois : un sujet pour réviser for/since/during, le present perfect et le son th.

sources.title: French, US and Russian astronauts return to Earth after eight months in space

facts.fact: Sophie Adenot (France, European Space Agency), Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway (NASA) and Andrey Fedyaev (Roscosmos) returned from the International Space Station on Thursday 8 October 2026.
Their SpaceX capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Los Angeles.
The mission lasted almost eight months. The crew launched in February 2026 on a Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral, Florida.
About 45 minutes before splashdown the capsule was travelling at roughly 17,500 mph; the heat shield faced temperatures of up to 3,500°F; four parachutes slowed it to about 16 mph.
Jessica Meir did four spacewalks, just over 27 hours in total. Sophie Adenot did three.
Adenot became the first French woman to walk in space.
The crew went up to replace a crew sent home early after NASA's Mike Fincke fell ill, described as NASA's first medical evacuation in 65 years of human spaceflight.
Their replacements arrived three weeks late because of capsule repairs.
The crew did dozens of experiments, including studies on stem cells, crystal growth and bone loss in microgravity.
Seven people (from the US, Russia and Canada) remain on the station.
Meir, after splashdown: 'We are so excited to be back on Planet Earth after an incredible mission on the International Space Station.'
Meir, before leaving: 'So looking forward to seeing nature again, feeling the breeze on my face, the wind rustling through the leaves.'
Meir said she would miss 'weightlessness and the wonderful views of Earth'.

reading.headline: Home at last: four astronauts end an eight-month mission
reading.standfirst: A SpaceX capsule has brought four astronauts, including France's Sophie Adenot, back from the International Space Station after almost eight months.
paragraphs: On Thursday 8 October, a SpaceX capsule dropped into the Pacific Ocean, off the coast of Los Angeles. Inside were four astronauts who had lived on the International Space Station for almost eight months: Americans Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, Russian Andrey Fedyaev and Sophie Adenot from France.

The last part of the journey was fast and tough. About 45 minutes before landing, the capsule was moving at roughly 17,500 mph, and its heat shield had to withstand temperatures of up to 3,500°F. Four parachutes then slowed it down to about 16 mph. After splashdown, Meir said the crew was "so excited to be back on Planet Earth after an incredible mission", according to AP.

This crew had an unusual story. They flew up in February to replace colleagues who were sent home early when NASA's Mike Fincke fell ill. AP described that as NASA's first medical evacuation in 65 years of human spaceflight. Later, the astronauts who were supposed to replace them arrived three weeks late because of repairs to their capsule, so the mission lasted longer than planned.

Life on board was busy. The crew carried out dozens of experiments, including studies on stem cells, crystal growth and bone loss. Meir completed four spacewalks, just over 27 hours outside the station in total. Adenot did three, and she became the first French woman to walk in space.

Before leaving, Meir said she was looking forward to "feeling the breeze on my face". She also said she would miss weightlessness and the wonderful views of Earth. Seven people from the US, Russia and Canada are still living on the station.
reading.credit: Written for learners from reports by France 24 (AP) and NPR, 8 October 2026

listening.title: Coffee break: who wants to live in space?
listening.contextFr: Deux collègues développeurs discutent à la pause café du retour des astronautes. Les personnages sont fictifs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Did you see the news this morning? The astronauts have finally come back after almost eight months in space.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yeah, I watched the splashdown video at my desk. I mean, I can't imagine it. The capsule was going at about seventeen thousand miles an hour, and then four parachutes slowed it down.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right, and the heat shield has to withstand incredibly high temperatures. Honestly, I'd be terrified.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Well, the best part is the story before that. They went up to replace another crew, because one astronaut fell ill and everyone had to come home early.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Really? I didn't know that. So they stayed longer than planned?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, because their replacements arrived three weeks late. Apparently, the astronaut Jessica Meir did four spacewalks during the mission.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Four! Actually, I read that the French astronaut, Sophie Adenot, did three, and she was the first French woman to walk in space.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's amazing. Would you do it, though? Eight months without a proper shower or a pizza?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hmm, I'm not sure. Weightlessness sounds fun for a week. But I'd really miss the rain, believe it or not. I'm British, after all.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ha, fair enough. Meir said she was looking forward to feeling the breeze on her face. Simple things, you know?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. After all those experiments, I think I'd just want a long walk and a cup of tea.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And no meetings for a week!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Don't push it, Jake. We have a sprint review at three.

vocabulary.instructionFr: Complétez avec le mot ou l'expression qui convient.

items.prompt: The capsule's ___ protects it from the heat when it re-enters the atmosphere.
items.explanationFr: Le « heat shield » est le bouclier thermique.

items.prompt: Two engineers ___ ill the day before the launch.
items.explanationFr: « fall ill » (prétérit : fell ill) = tomber malade.

items.prompt: I'm really ___ forward to my trip to London.
items.explanationFr: « look forward to » = avoir hâte de. Piège : on dit « to + -ing ».

items.prompt: Can you ___ down? I can't follow you when you speak so fast.
items.explanationFr: « slow down » = ralentir, aussi pour la parole.

items.prompt: Astronauts feel ___ in orbit, so everything floats.
items.explanationFr: « weightlessness » = apesanteur ; la phrase demande ici un nom : « feel weightlessness » fonctionne comme dans le texte.

vocabulary.instructionFr: Choisissez la bonne traduction. Attention aux faux amis et aux calques.

items.prompt: « Nous avons réalisé une étude » : We ___ a study.
items.explanationFr: « To realise » signifie « se rendre compte », pas « réaliser » une tâche.

items.prompt: « Actuellement, sept personnes sont sur la station » : ___, seven people are on the station.
items.explanationFr: « Actually » = en fait. « Actuellement » se traduit par « currently ».

items.prompt: « Ils vont remplacer l'équipage » : They will ___ the crew.
items.explanationFr: « Replace » prend un complément direct ; « remplace » n'existe pas en anglais.

items.prompt: « Le vaisseau résiste à la chaleur » : The ship ___ the heat.
items.explanationFr: « Resist to » est un calque ; « support » veut dire « soutenir ». On dit « withstand ».

items.prompt: « Il a quitté la station hier » : He ___ the station yesterday.
items.explanationFr: Avec « yesterday », on utilise le prétérit : « left ».

grammar.point: for, since, during + present perfect / past simple
grammar.explanationFr: « For » + durée (for eight months), « since » + point de départ (since February) : ils s'emploient avec le present perfect quand la situation continue (« have lived … for eight months »). « During » + nom d'une période ou d'un événement (during the mission) répond à « quand ? » et non « combien de temps ? ». Si l'action est terminée et datée, on emploie le prétérit : « They launched in February ». Piège français : « depuis » se traduit par « for » ou « since » selon qu'on donne une durée ou une date, jamais par « from ».
examples: The crew had lived on the station for almost eight months.
Meir completed four spacewalks during the mission.

items.prompt: The astronauts have been in space ___ February. [for / since / during]
She has worked for the space agency ___ ten years. [for / since / during]
Several experiments were done ___ the mission. [for / since / during]
They (live) on the station for eight months. [present perfect, they are still there]
They (land) in the Pacific yesterday. [past simple]

writing.taskFr: Un collègue britannique vous demande par message si vous aimeriez passer huit mois dans l'espace. Répondez-lui avec votre avis et deux raisons, en utilisant for, since ou during.
language: I've wanted to … since I was a child
criteria: Donner clairement son avis (oui/non) et le justifier
Utiliser au moins un for, since ou during correctement
writing.modelAnswer: Hi Tom! Honestly, I'm not sure I would go. Although the views of Earth must be amazing, I would miss simple things, like cooking dinner and walking in the rain. I've never lived away from home for more than a month, so eight months sounds too long for me! Also, I would be worried about the return, because the capsule travels very fast. During my holidays, I prefer a quiet beach! But I'd try one week, maybe. What about you?

speaking.taskFr: Parlez pendant 60 à 90 secondes : que feriez-vous en premier si vous reveniez sur Terre après huit mois dans l'espace, et pourquoi ?
prompts: What would you do first when you got back?
What would you miss from the station?
Would you like to try a spacewalk? Why or why not?
language: The first thing I would do is…
For eight months, I would have…
On the one hand… on the other hand…

pronunciation.tipFr: Le « ei » est long ; accent sur la première syllabe ; finale « -nəs » faible.
Le « th » est voisé : langue entre les dents, comme dans « this » ; accent sur « stand ».
Le « th » final est sourd : langue entre les dents, soufflez sans voix ; voyelle courte « ʌ ».
Mettez la langue entre les dents pour « th », puis un « r » anglais, sans le rouler.

speaking.modelAnswer: The first thing I would do is take a long, hot shower, because I'd have missed it for eight months. Then I would eat a big pizza with my family. I've always loved technology, so I would also miss the view of Earth from the window. On the other hand, I wouldn't want to do a spacewalk, because it seems very dangerous. But it must be an incredible experience, so I would try it once, with a very good team.
